articles.title: Gold Skulltulas - The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time Guide - IGN
articles.summary: Here is IGN's complete list of all 100 Gold Skulltulla locations in The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time and Ocarina of Time 3D. Killing each of these
articles.body:
Here is IGN's complete list of all 100 Gold Skulltulla locations in The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time and Ocarina of Time 3D. Killing each of these spiders throughout Hyrule drops a Gold Skulltula medallion that you can retrieve by touching or with an item like the Boomerang. The Gold Skulltula medallions can then be exchanged for prizes in the Skulltula House in Kakariko Village . We have a full list of rewards at the bottom of the page -- you get the best reward, Tap to Reveal by collecting only 30.

Replaying OOT before the remake comes out? Until November 5th, 2026 , you can use free, unlimited checkmarks on IGN's Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time guides, no subscription required!

This guide is verified and is the same for Ocarina of Time for Nintendo 64, the GameCube collector's edition disc, the remake on Nintendo 3DS, and the Nintendo Online versions for Nintendo Switch and Switch 2.

If you are looking for IGN's 2026 Switch 2 OOT Remake Gold Skulltula Locations, check out our The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time Remake Gold Skulltula Guide as the locations have changed slightly for some.

For Master Quest's altered Heart Piece locations, see: Master Quest Gold Skulltulla Locations

Here are all 100 Skulltula locations, in the order you're able to obtain them, in a trackable list. We have a video (above) and then a text walkthrough with screenshots and helpful checklists. You can use our interactive checklist feature to help you keep track of the ones you've already found. Simply mark off the ones you've collected to help you organize your play. Enjoy the very best guide to Gold Skulltulas on the web and happy hunting!

Gold Skulltula #1: Great Deku Tree (Child)

On the third floor, in the room where you obtain the compass, in a small hideaway on the left.

Gold Skulltula #2: Great Deku Tree (Child)

The next Skulltulla is crawling around on the vines on the cave wall after you fall through the giant web.

Gold Skulltula #3: Great Deku Tree (Child)

On the gate in the room you're in when you fall through giant web.

Gold Skulltula #4: Kokiri Forest (Child) (Night Only)

Back of Know-It-All-Brothers' house. Only appears at night.

Gold Skulltula #5: Hyrule Castle Town (Child)

In a crate in the room full of pots at the city gate. Enter the guardhouse and roll into the crate to smash it.

Gold Skulltula #6: Hyrule Castle (Child)

Run into the back area past the market place where you snuck into the Hyrule Castle. Roll into the first tree across from the vines.

Gold Skulltula #7: Lon Lon Ranch (Child)

In a tree near the corral where cuccos hang out during the day. Roll into the tree trunk and the Skulltula will pop out.

Gold Skulltula #8: Lon Lon Ranch (Child) (Night Only)

On the back of wooden part of the corral, north of the entrance. Appears at night only.

Gold Skulltula #9: Kakariko Village (Child) (Night Only)

In the large tree near the entrance. Roll into it and the Skulltula will drop down from the branches above. Appears at night only.

Gold Skulltula #10: Kakariko Village (Child) (Night Only)

On the side of the house across from the guard gate near Death Mountain pass. Appears at night only.

Gold Skulltula #11: Kakariko Village (Child) (Night Only)

On the watch tower ladder. Use the slingshot to kill it first, then climb up to claim the token. Appears at night only.

Gold Skulltula #12: Kakariko Village (Child) (Night Only)

On one of the brick walls at the incomplete house. Appears at night only.

Gold Skulltula #13: Kakariko Village (Child)

On the side of the cursed Skulltula house.

Gold Skulltula #14: Kakariko Graveyard (Child)

Release some bugs on the soft soil patch. You can find bugs under a rock to the right of the graveyard entrance. Appears at night only.

Gold Skulltula #15: Kokiri Forest (Child)

Release a bug from a bottle and let it crawl into the soft soil near the Kokiri shop.

From the entrance of the Lost Woods , take two lefts. Plant a bug in the soft soil in the area with the bridge.

From the entrance, go right, left, right, left, then left and find the soft soil under the Deku Scrub.

Gold Skulltula #18: Death Mountain Trail (Child)

Plant a bug in the soft soil in front of the entrance to Dodongo's Cavern .

Gold Skulltula #19: Dodongo's Cavern (Child)

In the room with the exploding Dodongo larvae, just off the side of the main hall, lead the larvae to the breakable wall and attack them -- They will explode and blow the wall open (you could also use a bomb). Beyond the wall is a room with some Keese and a Gold Skulltula.

Gold Skulltula #20: Dodongo's Cavern (Child)

In the "stairway" room, with the ring of bombs around a large column, set off the bombs to bring down the stairs. Climb the stairs and look on the vines by the door to the second floor for a Skulltula.

Gold Skulltula #21: Dodongo's Cavern (Child)

In the room before the boss, inside the Dodongo mouth, there is a wall you can destroy that leads to a room with the Skulltula. The breakable wall is in the room with the gray, push-able blocks.

Gold Skulltula #22: Death Mountain Trail (Child)

Bomb the cracked wall at the bottom of the trail near the entrance to Kakariko Village to reveal secret cave. You can clearly see the bombable portion on the right side of the rock wall when heading up, in the area that you're fighting Tektites or defending yourself from rolling boulders.

Gold Skulltula #23: Death Mountain Crater (Child)

Inside Death Mountain Crater. Climb Death Mountain and enter the Death Mountain Crater. Break open the box on the inside.

Inside Goron City. Break the crate on the top floor (in the same room with the different colored rocks).

Gold Skulltula #25: Zora River (Child) (Night Only)

In the first tree you see when you enter the river. Roll into the tree to bring it down. Appears at night only.

On the ladder near the entrance to Zora's Domain .

Gold Skulltula #27: Zora's Fountain (Child)

In the tree on the small shore opposite the entrance. Roll into the tree to bring it down.

Gold Skulltula #28: Inside Jabu-Jabu's Belly (Child)

On the vines in the room where you raise the water level.

Gold Skulltula #29: Inside Jabu-Jabu's Belly (Child)

In the room after falling through the long pit.

Gold Skulltula #30: Inside Jabu-Jabu's Belly (Child)

Right next to the previous Gold Skulltula in the same room.

Gold Skulltula #31: Inside Jabu-Jabu's Belly (Child)

Gold Skulltula #32: Zora's Fountain (Child) (Night Only)

To the right of the fallen log in the water is a Skulltula hanging on the wall. It appears only at night.

Gold Skulltula #33: Great Deku Tree (Child)

Behind the only bombable wall in the room with the Gohma larva. Bomb the wall, kill the Skulltula, and use the boomerang to get the token.

Gold Skulltula #34: Dodongo's Cavern (Child)

n the "stairway" room, with the ring of bombs around a large set of stairs. Above the large set of stairs is a nook with the Skulltula. Go to the second floor bridge that leads to the second floor of the room with the stairs to reach it. Go to the west side and leap to the stairs. You can reach the Skulltula from the nook with your weapons. You can also return here as an Adult and use the Longshot to reach it instead.

Gold Skulltula #35: Lon Lon Ranch (Child) (Night Only)

Boomerang required! On the side of Talon's house, on one of the windows at the top. Appears at night only.

Gold Skulltula #36: Lon Lon Ranch (Child) (Night Only)

Boomerang required! High up on the wooden wall to the left of the cow shed. Appears at night only.

Gold Skulltula #37: Kakariko Graveyard (Child) (Night Only)

Boomerang required! On the wall to the right opposite side of the entrance.

Gold Skulltula #38: Hyrule Field (Either Era)

After crossing the bridge going from Hyrule castle to Kakariko village, place a bomb next to the tree at the walls of Hyrule castle. This will open a hole containing a regular Skulltula and the Gold Skulltula.

Gold Skulltula #39: Hyrule Field (Either Era)

Requires the Boomerang or Hookshot, and Din's Fire.

Find the ring of rocks near the entrance to Gerudo Valley and place a bomb in the center of the rock ring, then drop down into the hole. Use Din's fire to clear out the cobwebs preventing access to the cow. The Skulltula is in the same chamber.

Gold Skulltula #40: Gerudo Valley (Child) (Night Only)

Look to the right of the plank leading into the area from Hyrule field. The Skulltula is hanging over the small waterfall.

Gold Skulltula #41: Gerudo Valley (Child)

Look to the right side of the gate on the bridge and you'll see a ledge far below. Jump to the ledge using the cucco and plant a bug in the Soft Soil by the Gerudo with a cow.

Plant bugs in the soft soil next to the lab.

Gold Skulltula #43: Lake Hylia (Child) (Night Only)

Gold Skulltula #44: Lake Hylia (Child) (Night Only)

On the small island with the two pillars (in the same place where you get the Fire Arrows).

Gold Skulltula #45: Ganon's Castle (Adult)

Find this Skulltula on the back of the arch that used to be the guard gate. Use the Hookshot to get to it, or climb up to it, being careful not to jump off the ledge.

Gold Skulltula #46: Kakariko Village (Adult) (Night Only)

On the wall on the roof of Impa's House, the house next to the chicken pen. Use the Hookshot or Longshot to get up there.

Gold Skulltula #47: Kokiri Forest (Adult) (Night Only)

Back of the Twins' House. Use the Hookshot to get the token. Only appears at night.

Gold Skulltula #48: Lost Woods (Adult) (Night Only)

Go right, left, right, left, and left then ride the magic bean platform (plant bean as child first). Appears at night only.

Gold Skulltula #49: Sacred Forest Meadow (Adult) (Night Only)

Found in the Sacred Forest Meadow , at night only. This Skulltula is hanging on the wall just above the maze of Moblins. You'll need the Hookshot to grab the Token.

Gold Skulltula #50: Forest Temple (Adult)

To the right of the entrance on the vines.

Gold Skulltula #51: Forest Temple (Adult)

Gold Skulltula #52: Forest Temple (Adult)

In the West outdoor room on the wall. Look for the wooden chest up on the platform and target it with your hookshot. The Skulltula is to the left, on the wall.

Gold Skulltula #53: Forest Temple (Adult)

Gold Skulltula #54: Forest Temple (Adult)

Gold Skulltula #55: Bottom of the Well (Child)

As young Link, check out the wall in the room behind the left door in the center. Boomerang required.

Gold Skulltula #56: Bottom of the Well (Child)

In the room behind the right locked door.

Gold Skulltula #57: Bottom of the Well (Child)

Crawl through the small opening in the northeast.

Gold Skulltula #58: Hyrule Castle (Child)

Requires the Bombs, Boomerang, and Song of Storms.

Go past the guards through the castle moat. Play the Song of Storms near the lone tree to make a hole in the ground appear. Go inside and listen for the Skulltula. Bomb the back, left wall inside the hole.

Inside Goron City. On the side of the small platform that once held the Stone of Fire in the middle of Goron City .

In the room with the long bridge, move the blue Time Block by playing the Song of Time. Climb on top and go through the door to find a room with a Like-Like and the Skulltula.

Find this Skulltula in the maze room, behind a destructible wall. To find it, enter the maze and turn left, left, right, and then straight -- the bomb the wall.

On the second floor of the maze room in the Fire Temple, Navi will fly up and turn green. Play the Scarecrow Song and Hookshot up to Pierre to find the Skulltula.

Immediately after the previous Gold Skulltula, climb up to find a door. The next Skulltula is on the wall above the pit, in the other big donut-shaped room on the map, opposite the one where you find the Megaton Hammer.

In the room before you get the Boss Key -- accessible after you whack away the layers of the statue blocking the way. The room features flying tiles and a Like-Like.

Gold Skulltula #65: Death Mountain Trail (Adult) (Night Only)

This Skulltula is on the wall of the path where the falling rocks pelt you as a child. As an adult there are no rocks, so you'll have safe passage. The Skulltula appears right before the scalable cliff wall. Appears at night only.

Gold Skulltula #66: Death Mountain Trail (Adult) (Night Only)

Go to where the bomb plant was used to open Dodongo's Cavern (above the cavern entrance) and break the nearby rock open with your hammer. Only appears when it is night time.

Gold Skulltula #67: Dodongo's Cavern (Adult)

In the room with the exploding Dodongo larvae, just off the side of the main hall, Navi will fly up to the upper area and turn green. Play the Scarecrow's Song in the middle of the room and Pierre will appear. Hookshot up to the scarecrow and you'll find the Skulltula.

Gold Skulltula #68: Death Mountain Crater (Child)

Plant a bug in the soft soil inside Death Mountain Crater (use Bolero of Fire to reach the area).

Climb up the ladder on the small ledge on the way down the river to get to the Fairy Fountain above the river. Near the Fairy Fountain you'll see a circle of rocks and one big rock in the middle. Turn to the left of these rocks and find the Skulltula hanging on the wall.

Look up high on the left wall after the bridge that leads to the waterfall. You can use the Longshot to reach it, or if you climb up on the fence, it can be reached with the Hookshot.

Gold Skulltula #71: Zora's Domain (Adult) (Night Only)

Stand on the edge of the bottom of the frozen waterfall and shoot the Skulltula high up on the wall near the top of the falls. Has to be night before going in otherwise it won't appear.

In the room with the large rotating blade.

In the room East of the rotating blade, where you obtained the Compass.

In the room with the moving blocks of ice.

At the bottom of the Lake Hylia lab in a crate. Iron Boots needed.

Gold Skulltula #76: Water Temple (Adult)

Start in the main room with the water completely drained and follow the tunnel that leads to a dead-end with a weakened floor. Drop a bomb on the floor and swim to a new room. Hit the switch and Hookshot to the platform. The diamond switch controls the gate -- do a spin attack to trigger it and open the gate and you'll find the Gold Skulltula on the wall.

Gold Skulltula #77: Water Temple (Adult)

In the cavern with the underground river, equip the Iron Boots and look for the Skulltula on the wall above the second vortex.

Gold Skulltula #78: Water Temple (Adult)

In the waterlogged room with the rolling boulders, look for the Skulltula behind the flowing water on the west wall of the narrow tunnel.

Gold Skulltula #79: Water Temple (Adult)

After acquiring the Longshot, head to the main tower in the center of the central hub area of the temple. Enter it when the water level is set to low, then Hookshot up, play Zelda's Lullaby to raise the water level and climb on the platform. Look up -- the Skulltula is high up under the ceiling and can be taken out with the Longshot.

Gold Skulltula #80: Water Temple (Adult)

Raise the water level in the main chamber to its highest level. Head through the doorway at the top with the Hookshot target above it. The Skultulla is in the room with the platforms and the waterfalls. Look for it on the right wall, reachable after obtaining the Longshot Hookshot.

Gold Skulltula #81: Lake Hylia (Adult) (Night Only)

Shoot the trunk above the tree branch of the dead tree to land on the branch itself. Kill the Skulltula on the trunk by standing at the edge of the branch and hitting it with your hookshot (tree is located by warp point to the Water Temple).

Gold Skulltula #82: Shadow Temple (Adult)

After fighting the Stalfos skeleton on the floating platform, use your Lens of Truth to see platforms going to a door on the left. This leads to a large, seemingly empty space, but you'll be mysteriously hurt. A quick look through the Lens reveals invisible, rotating scythes. Kill all the Keese and the Like Like in the room to unlock the gate to access the Gold Skulltula.

Gold Skulltula #83: Shadow Temple (Adult)

In a cage in the room with the falling spikes.

Gold Skulltula #84: Shadow Temple (Adult)

In the same room as the single giant skull head.

Gold Skulltula #85: Shadow Temple (Adult)

Stand at the tip of the ghost ship and use the Longshot to reach the Skulltula in the upper left.

Gold Skulltula #86: Shadow Temple (Adult)

Gold Skulltula #87: Gerudo Valley (Adult) (Night Only)

Appears at night only. Behind the Carpenters' tent.

Gold Skulltula #88: Gerudo Valley (Adult)

On backside of stone pillar across from carpenters' tent.

Gold Skulltula #89: Gerudo Fortress (Adult) (Night Only)

High up on the dirt wall above center entrance to fort buildings. Night only.

Gold Skulltula #90: Gerudo Fortress (Adult)

On the target pole at the archery range.

Gold Skulltula #91: Haunted Wasteland (Adult)

Inside the small building where you find the phantom guide.

Gold Skulltula #92: Desert Colossus (Adult) (Night Only)

On a palm tree near the drained fairy pool outside the Spirit Temple.

Gold Skulltula #93: Desert Colossus (Child)

Find the soft soil next to the entrance of the Spirit Temple and plant a bug in it.

Gold Skulltula #94: Desert Colossus (Adult) (Night Only)

Ride the magic bean platform to small plateau top with this Skulltula on it (plant bean as child first).

Gold Skulltula #95: Spirit Temple (Child)

Crawl through the small hole at the beginning as young Link. Go through the door on the right side and look on the fence.

Gold Skulltula #96: Spirit Temple (Child)

Inside of the door through the second small hole (on other side of climbable wall).

Gold Skulltula #97: Spirit Temple (Child)

Above the door in the room that unlocks after you push the block under the sun light (as a child).

Gold Skulltula #98: Spirit Temple (Adult)

Use the Song of Time to move the blue box in the room with the silver rupees and boulders.

Gold Skulltula #99: Spirit Temple (Adult)

Across from the door that unlocks when you push the Armos on the switch in the room with the huge statue. Head up the stairs you ascended as Child Link and use your Longshot to reach it in the northwest corner. You can also use the Scarecrow Song to make it easier.

Gold Skulltula #100: Zora's Fountain (Adult) (Night Only)

At night time, on the far shore, blow up the rocks with a Bomb to reveal the Fairy Cave. One silver rock here requires Silver Gauntlets to lift. Remove it and blow up the boulder below it. Drop down and then run past the invisible Skulltulas using the Eye of Truth. Climb the ladder and the Skulltula is at the top.

Congrats, you've got them all! You can mark this optional sidequest complete:

Take your Gold Skulltula medallions to the Kakariko Village Skulltula house, right in the center/west side of town, to exchange them for rewards.

These tips are helpful for Skulltula hunting on Ocarina of Time:

Turn up the volume. Skulltulas make a scratching sound that helps you locate them. If you hear something but don't see something, that means the spider is behind a bombable wall or inside a container.

Skulltulas hidden in crates can be released by rolling into the cate or smashing it with the Hammer or blowing it up with a bomb.

Skulltulas in trees or on certain walls will drop when you roll into the tree trunks or walls/fences.

Some Skulltulas are hiding in the the soil patches with the holes on the them. To get them to come out, you need to first capture some bugs in a Bottle, then stand on the patch and release the bugs.

Killing Skulltulas is just half the story: you also need to retrieve the Skulltula Token. To reach the higher-up ones, use the boomerang or Hookshot. Some barely-out-of-reach ones can also be grabbed by using Link's backflip or forward slash jump (when locked on).

Some Skulltulas will require the help of the Scarecrow to reach. Teach an easily memorable song to the Scarecrow at Lake Hylia as Young Link, then return and play that same Scarecrow's song for them as an adult. If you ever notice Navi mysteriously glow green over a distant location, play the Scarecrow's Song to summon a hookshot target.

articles.title: Heart Pieces - The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time Guide - IGN
articles.summary: This guide covers the Heart Piece locations in the The Legend Of Zelda Ocarina Of Time. There are a total of 36 Pieces of Heart in this game. Every time you
articles.body:
This guide covers the Heart Piece locations in the The Legend Of Zelda Ocarina Of Time. There are a total of 36 Pieces of Heart in this game. Every time you gather four Pieces of Heart you will get a Heart Container, which adds another Heart to your total Health bar. Find all of the heart pieces to add nine Heart Containers to your total Health. The remaining Heart Containers come from beating bosses. This guide is verified and is the same for Ocarina of Time for Nintendo 64, the GameCube collector's edition disc, the remake on Nintendo 3DS, and the Nintendo Online versions for Nintendo Switch and Switch 2.

If you are looking for IGN's 2026 Switch 2 OOT Remake Heart Piece Locations, check out our The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time Remake Heart Pieces Guide as the locations have changed slightly for some.

For the Nintendo 3DS Master Quest's altered Heart Piece locations, see: Master Quest Heart Piece Locations

Replaying OOT before the remake comes out? Until November 5th, 2026 , you can use free, unlimited checkmarks on IGN's Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time guides, no subscription required!

Heart Piece 1: Castle Town Market Alley Dog (Child)

During the night, find Richard the puppy and return him to his owner in the alley. Look for a white dog near the bazaar in the corner of the main market square and run around it in a circle a few times to get it to follow you back to the lady owner.

Heart Piece 2: Lon Lon Ranch Corner Tower (Child)

In the brick cow shed behind the corral (it looks like a tower in one corner of the ranch). Pull the boxes out revealing a path to a tunnel leading to the Heart Piece.

Heart Piece 3: Kakariko Graveyard Gravestone (Child)

The fourth tombstone in the top row from the right can be pushed back. Inside, play the Sun's Song to eliminate the Re-Dead, then play the Sun's Song once again and collect this piece from the chest that appears.

Heart Piece 4: Kakariko Graveyard Dampé Tour (Child)

Take part in Dampe’s Grave-digging Tour and have him dig in a patch of dirt. This is a random drop so it may take a while to find the Heart Piece. To get Dampe to dig, be sure you aren't wearing a mask and simply talk to him when he's over a patch of soil as he makes his rounds. It must be in the evening, but BEFORE midnight. The exact hours of Dampe's tour are on his door.

Heart Piece 5: Kakariko Village Rooftop Man (Child/Adult)

Speak to the man on the high rooftop, which can easily be reached by the Longshot . It's actually possible to reach it with the Hookshot by standing on the corner of the fence by the windmill entrance and moving around until you can get a bit of roof in your sites.

It is possible to side jump as a child onto the roof to get the Heart Piece early: As a child. Climb up the watch tower, and hug the upper-left corner. While Z-Targeting, leap to the left. If you lined up correctly, Link should land either directly on the rooftop, or on the thin fence next to it. Climb up onto the roof, and speak to the man, to get the Piece of Heart.

Heart Piece 6: Kakariko Village Impa's House Cow (Child)

In Impa's House there's a caged area with cow in it (it can be reached via the ledge above the Cucco pen outside of house). To get here you can ride the owl down from the summit of Death Mountain , then fall off the side of the roof to a platform. This takes you inside the caged area. However, you can do this much earlier in the game by climbing the construction project adjacent to the cucco pen with a cucco. Toss it on the ledges as you climb and carefully jump onto the beam with the construction worker as he runs away from you. Run off the beam and float to the ledge.

Heart Piece 7: Lost Woods Skull Kid Ocarina Game (Child)

From the entrance to the Lost Woods, head to the right once, and drop down off the ledge. Stand on the tree stump, and pull out your ocarina to perform with the two skull kids. Successfully repeat their song three times, with each reward better than the last, and you’ll receive a Piece of Heart.

Heart Piece 8: Lost Woods Skull Kid Serenade (Child)

From the entrance to the Lost Woods, head to the left once, and stand on the stump opposite the solo Skull Kid. Play Saria’s Song, and you will be rewarded with a Piece of Heart!

Heart Piece 9: Goron City Spinning Pot (Child)

After opening access to Darunia's room, light the torches around the giant urn in the middle of the city. Once the large pot is moving, throw a bomb in the top opening. The spinning pot must randomly stop on the happy face to get the heart piece.

Heart Piece 10: Death Mountain Trail Magic Bean (Child/Adult)

The 'correct' way to get this is to use the magic bean platform at entrance to Dodongo’s Cavern (plant a Magic Bean in the Soft Soil in front of the cavern as child first). However, you can get this much earlier as Kid Link by back-flipping off of the ledge above the heart piece. This ledge has a fence and a bomb plant. Back-flip at an angle towards the heart piece over the lower section of fence (you need to use targeting mode to back flip, do not target the bomb).

Heart Piece 11: Death Mountain Crater Wall (Child)

Enter Death Mountain Crater as a child without the Red Tunic and you'll have a short time limit before you get booted out (or fried). However, you do have just enough time to get the heart piece on the ledge far below the entrance and then climb out and run to safety. Run and roll to the cliff edge from the entrance and then climb down. A nook in this cliff holds the heart piece. Climb quickly back out and run to safety.

Heart Piece 12: Hyrule Field Lake Hylia Entrance Hole (Child/Adult)

In the little square of fence right at the entrance to Lake Hylia there is a secret hole that shows up if you have the Shard of Agony . You can also grab this Heart Piece without the stone, though. Plant a bomb square in the middle of the fenced-off area. Buy the heart piece from the business scrub for 10 rupees.

Heart Piece 13: Castle Town Market Bombchu Bowling (Child)

This will show up randomly as a prize in the Bombchu Bowling Game . Beat the Bombchu Bowling Game again to win it. You can also win a Bomb Bag upgrade and Bombchus in this game. This takes a bit of luck. For the first, closest targets on the sides or center, stand in front of them and aim straight for them. For the rest, angle your Bombchu towards the wall at various angles and make adjustments accordingly. Make sure you avoid the cuccos that will get in your way. You should SAVE before playing the game and reload the game if you run out of money and have no prizes to show for your 30 rupee efforts.

Heart Piece 14: Zora's River Cucco Flight (Child)

Take a cucco past the Singing Frogs up the two small ledges -- you'll have to toss the cucco onto a ledge and quickly run across the shallow stream to pick it up again. Instead of continuing upstream to Zora's Domain look downstream for a ledge by the cliff wall with a ladder. This leads to an upper area with a hole leading to a Fairy Fountain . Fly with the chicken over to the ledge and leave it behind once you land safely. Climb up the ladder and find a new cucco at the top. Locate the visible heart container and fly over to it.

Heart Piece 15: Zora's River Waterfall (Child)

With the same cucco from the bottom of the area, go to the entrance of Zora’s Domain. Fly off the ledge with the Triforce Seal and land on the nearby heart piece.

Heart Piece 16: Zora's Domain Torches (Child)

Light the torches in the cave under the waterfall by carrying fire down from the royal chamber. You'll need a Deku Stick for this. First light the stone torch on the stairs so it stays lit. Carry fire from it to the torch in front of the shop, then run from there out onto the shallow water to light another torch. From here, run behind the waterfall and quickly light the final two torches to reveal a chest with a Heart Piece.

Heart Piece 17: Gerudo Valley Crate (Child/Adult)

The Heart Piece is located on a small cliff above the water. On the side opposite the carpenter's tent, drop off the ledge (as far to the left of the "no diving" sign as you can get). Walk to the grey boulder, then Longshot to the box on the opposite side. Alternatively, you can also use a Cucco to fly off of the left side of the carpenters bridge and land on the right ledge with said crate. Roll into the crate to find a Piece of Heart.

Heart Piece 18: Gerudo Valley Waterfall (Child/Adult)

As a child, plant a magic bean in the soft soil along the cliff. Ride the platform as an adult and head through the waterfall. Alternatively, as a kid you may use a Cucco to fly off the side of the bridge and into the compartment within the waterfall. Alternatively, you can also use the Iron Boots and Longshot to get the Piece of Heart. On the same side as the carpenter's tent, drop off the north most portion of the ledge, onto the ledge below. Jump into the water and immediately equip the Iron Boots. Walk north towards the waterfall, and Longshot up to the ladder. Climb the ladder.

Heart Piece 19: Lake Hylia Fishing Pond Lunker (Child)

Go fishing in the Fishing Pond and catch a fish that’s around 10 pounds, or a "lunker," as the owner describes it. The fish should be near the log that is emerging from the water. Get the store owner to weigh it and he will give you a heart piece.

Heart Piece 20: Kakariko Graveyard Magic Bean (Child/Adult)

Ride magic bean platform as an adult (you must plant a Magic Bean in the Soft Soil just to the left as you enter the graveyard as a kid) and smash the crate. Alternatively, you can Longshot to the crate.

Heart Piece 21: Kakariko Village Windmill (Adult)

Inside the windmill there is a heart piece on a wooden platform. You must complete Dampe's race in Kakariko Graveyard to get to this upper area of the windmill -- although once you have the Hookshot from winning the race it's easy to get up here. You can get this heart piece much earlier using the boomerang as a child. This is a very difficult maneuver.

Heart Piece 22: Kakariko Graveyard Dampé Race (Adult)

Win against Dampe in a second race under his grave, finishing in a minute or less. Roll when you have Dampe in sight to move faster, but don't roll when he's out of sight around corners or you'll likely get fried by his fire. When you get to the final room in the race, Longshot to the torch at the top of the room for maximum results.

Heart Piece 23: Zora's River Frogs (Child)

Play the Song of Storms song to the Singing Frogs under the water by the log to receive a heart piece.

Heart Piece 24: Zora's River Frogs Bug Game (Child)

In addition to playing the Song of Storms to the frogs and obtaining that heart piece, play the rest of the non-warp songs for the frog choir. Each one will make the frogs grow. After completing all six songs, stay in your same position and pull your ocarina out again. The family of frogs pop out onto the logs. They will each represent a note and sort of play an on-the-go simon says game with you. Get to the end of their puzzle (all frogs inflated), and you will receive another Heart Piece! The sequence gets pretty tough, so here it is made easy:

Nintendo 3DS: L, X, Y, R, X, Y, R, L, R, L, R, Y, X, L- Nintendo 64: A C-Left, C-Right, C-Down, C-Left, C-Right, C-Down, A, C-Down, A, C-Down, C-Right, C-Left, A.

Heart Piece 25: Castle Town Market Treasure Chest Game (Child)

Complete the treasure chest guessing game. Using the Lens of Truth(from the bottom of the well ) will allow you to cheat in this game.

Heart Piece 26: Kakariko Village House of Skulltula Reward (Child/Adult)

After you have 50 skulltulas , go to the House of Skulltula in Kakariko village and claim your prize.

Heart Piece 27: Lake Hylia Lab Chimney (Child/Adult)

On top of laboratory is a tall chimney with this heart piece at the top. Plant a Magic Bean in the Soft Soil in front of the Laboratory as a child to get up to the chimney.

Heart Piece 28: Death Mountain Crater Spike (Child/Adult)

Ride the magic bean platform inside of the Death Mountain Crater to this heart piece on the tip of a spire in the crater. The Soft Soil is located near the warp platform, and you'll need the Bolero of Fire to reach this area as a kid. Warp back out after you plant your Magic Bean .

Heart Piece 29: Zora's Fountain Iceberg (Adult)

In Zora's fountain, this heart piece is located on one of the unstable icebergs.

Heart Piece 30: Ice Cavern Red Ice (Adult)

Right at the entrance there's a room with a spinning blade. A clump of red stalagmites here can be melted with blue flame. Enter the room behind this to find the Heart Piece.

Heart Piece 31: Zora's Fountain Bottom (Adult)

When you have the iron boots, equip them to sink to the bottom of the lake floor under the icebergs. The Heart Piece will be in the center.

Heart Piece 32: Hyrule Field Northwest Tree Hole (Adult)

Detonate a bomb next to the lone tree in the northwest corner of Hyrule Field, near Lon-Lon Ranch. Your Shard of Agony should reveal this location. Drop into the hole in the ground next to the tree and then use the Iron Boots to sink underwater and reach the Heart.

Heart Piece 33: Lake Hylia Laboratory Dive (Adult)

Get the Gold Diving Scale from the Fishing Pond owner (by catching a 15lb fish as an adult in the same place as the 10 lb as a child) and go to the Laboratory. Dive and touch the bottom of the pool in the Laboratory. Talk to the old man to retrieve a Heart Piece.

Heart Piece 34: Gerudo Fortress Rooftop (Adult)

At the very top of the buildings there is a chest you can longshot to after saving all of the carpenters or you can use the Scarecrow's Song to summon him and use him as a hookshot target.

Heart Piece 35: Gerudo Fortress Horseback Archery (Adult)

Win the first round of the horseback archery range with a score of 1000+.

Heart Piece 36: Desert Colossus Magic Bean (Child/Adult)

Plant a magic bean at the Desert Colossus as a kid. Ride the magic bean platform to the end of the ride and jump to the heart piece as an adult.

Up Next: Master Quest Heart Piece Locations

articles.summary: Your adventurous journey has led you to the Hammerlocke Gym page of IGN’s Pokemon Sword and Shield walkthrough and wiki guide. This page contains info
articles.body:
Your adventurous journey has led you to the Hammerlocke Gym page of IGN’s Pokemon Sword and Shield walkthrough and wiki guide. This page contains info on hidden collectible locations, appearance rates for any wild Pokemon , and a strategy to navigate towards the Dragon Badge - Hammerlocke Gym .

Reach the front of the stadium to see a gathering of some of the more important characters in the story. And yay! Granny Magnolia is back! After some chatting, head north and into the stadium.

Nothing here to pick up or find, not even from Ball Guy! Just talk to the guy at the end of the hallway. Get dressed, then you'll be taken the Vault where you'll be tasked to fight in double battles.

First up is Gym Trainer Sebatian. He's got a Sliggoo and Pelipper . The Sliggoo is a pure Dragon type, so fight back with a Dragon move, yes the same type, or with Ice or Fairy . Pelipper can be taken quickly with an Electric move.

Next up is Gym Trainer Camilla. Her Ninetales is weak to Water and Ground and her Turtonator , despite being a Fire and Dragon type, will also take damage from a Fire move, and is also weak to Ground .

And finally we have Gym Trainer Aria. For this one we're up against an Abomasnow and Hakamo-o . The Abomasnow is a Grass and Ice type so a Fire attack would absolutely wreck it. A Fairy attack is highly recommended on the Hakamo-o.

And now it's time for the true battle. Just like the gym mission battles, the gym leader battle will be a doubles fight!

Gigalith and Flygon are up first and they're pretty different in terms of what they're weak to. Water , Grass , Fighting , Ground , and Steel all work for the Gigalith while an Ice attack on the Flygon is super effective. Same situation for the Sandaconda and Duraludon . Water , Grass , and Ice works quite nicely for Sandaconda while a Fighting and Ground attack is great against Duraludon .

The Dragon Badge, it's yours! In addition to completing the Gym Challenge, you also get to keep your Dragon Uniform, the TM99 Breaking Swipe , and you are now able to catch any Pokemon, no matter the level! Neat! There's also a new item in the shop:

Exit the stadium to find Sonia and Professor Magnolia right across the bridge. After Sonia levels up to a professor, head for the train station down the right path to start your journey towards Wyndon . Enter inside and you'll have a thankfully quick chat with Hop and Raihan before jumping onto the train. This will take you to Route 10 !

Up Next: Champion Gym Challenge - Wyndon Gym

articles.title: GTA VI no Xbox One? Veja em quais consoles será possível jogar  | G1
articles.standfirst: Rockstar confirma que GTA VI poderá ser jogado no Xbox One por meio do Xbox Cloud Gaming, que permite jogar via nuvem, além de chegar ao PlayStation 5 e ao Xbox Series X|S.
articles.summary: Rockstar confirma que GTA VI poderá ser jogado no Xbox One por meio do Xbox Cloud Gaming, que permite jogar via nuvem, além de chegar ao PlayStation 5 e ao Xbox Series X|S.
articles.body:
GTA IV vai rodar no Xbox One. — Foto: Divulgação/Rockstar Games

Nesta terça-feira (10), a Rockstar Games liberou o pré-carregamento de Grand Theft Auto VI ( GTA VI ) para jogadores que reservaram o game digitalmente. Junto ao anúncio, a empresa confirmou as plataformas em que o título poderá ser jogado: PlayStation 5, Xbox Series X|S e Xbox One.

Jogar GTA VI no Xbox One , um console da geração anterior, é uma novidade. No entanto, para aproveitar o game, os jogadores terão de acessar pelo Xbox Cloud Gaming , serviço de jogos por streaming da Microsoft. Nesse modelo, o título é executado em servidores remotos, e o console recebe a transmissão pela internet, sem precisar instalar o jogo no aparelho.

Segundo a Microsoft, o acesso pelo Xbox Cloud Gaming estará disponível desde o primeiro dia, a partir das 3h (horário de Brasília).

Apesar da possibilidade de jogar no Xbox One, o aparelho não receberá uma versão nativa do game. A transmissão utilizará as configurações gráficas do Xbox Series S.

Como jogar GTA 6 no Xbox One pela nuvem?

O Xbox Cloud Gaming permite executar jogos em servidores da Microsoft e transmiti-los para dispositivos compatíveis. Dessa forma, o processamento do game não depende da capacidade do console.

Na prática, quem tem um Xbox One poderá abrir o serviço, acessar GTA 6 e jogar com o controle do aparelho. O console funcionará como uma tela que recebe a transmissão do jogo e envia os comandos do usuário.

A Microsoft informou que, a partir de 11 de novembro, jogadores em mercados onde o recurso estiver disponível também poderão comprar tempo de jogo na nuvem para transmitir títulos compatíveis sem uma assinatura do Game Pass.

O jogo precisará ser comprado separadamente. A disponibilidade do serviço, as opções de compra e a elegibilidade das contas podem variar conforme o mercado e o dispositivo.

GTA 6 terá gráficos de Xbox Series S no Xbox One

De acordo com a Rockstar, a transmissão pelo Xbox Cloud Gaming utilizará as configurações gráficas do Xbox Series S. Isso significa que o jogador não terá exatamente a mesma experiência visual de quem executa o título nativamente em um Xbox Series X ou em um PlayStation 5 Pro.

A empresa também informou que GTA 6 foi desenvolvido para aproveitar a capacidade dos consoles da geração atual, com foco em uma taxa de 30 quadros por segundo (FPS).

No PlayStation 5 Pro, o game terá recursos gráficos adicionais, como maior nitidez por meio da tecnologia PSSR (PlayStation Spectral Super Resolution) e sombras com traçado de raios (ray tracing).

Já no PlayStation 5, o jogo contará com recursos táteis integrados ao controle DualSense, áudio espacial Tempest 3D e tempos de carregamento aprimorados.

O lançamento do GTA VI está marcado para 19 de novembro de 2026. O jogo chega inicialmente para PlayStation 5 e Xbox Series X|S, com possibilidade de acesso pelo Xbox One por meio do serviço de jogos em nuvem da Microsoft.

A Rockstar Games ainda não anunciou uma data de lançamento para PC.

articles.title: What DC Movies and Shows Could Get Batgirl'd Next?
articles.summary: Don’t assume everything James Gunn and Peter Safran had planned at DC Studios will see the light of day.
articles.body:
And just like that, James Gunn and Peter Safran are done as the bosses at DC Studios. Fans are reeling from the news – some are bummed out, some are psyched , and others just have whiplash from the constant moves at the studio (and its parent, Warner Bros.) over the past decade. But one of the biggest questions that has immediately come to mind for most of us is what does this mean for the slate of movies and TV shows that the co-CEOs already had in the works?

Let’s not forget, the corporate overseers at Warner Bros. have dumped projects in the past, even when they were high-profile movies that had already been shot, like Coyote vs. Acme and, most infamously, Batgirl , a film that to this day has still not seen the light of day.

Is it possible that movies and series already in production under Gunn and Safran could now get the Batgirl treatment, be it for tax reasons, cost-saving measures, or even a creative overhaul in terms of the bigger DCU mission statement under new management? Certainly anything is possible these days in a world where Skydance somehow now owns Paramount and Warner Bros.! Let’s look at some of the key projects that we know were pretty far along in development at the time of the Gunn/Safran announcement, and what their chances of actually being released are.

And a quick note: Typically, specific production timelines on movies and TV shows are not public information, but reports from reputable outlets that cover the industry will often have reliable information on a project’s status.

Gunn’s follow-up to his Superman solo movie from last year, Man of Tomorrow has already been shot and is currently in post-production. This is essentially the Avengers of Gunn’s DCU in that it reportedly features pretty much every superhero we’ve met in this world so far, with a cast that includes Milly Alcock (Supergirl), Aaron Pierre (John Stewart), Edi Gathegi (Mister Terrific), Nathan Fillion (Guy Gardner), Isabela Merced (Hawkgirl), and even Xolo Maridueña (Blue Beetle), who is a holdover from the old DCEU!

As part of the announcement today about Gunn and Safran’s departure as co-CEOs, the studio made sure to mention that the pair would still be overseeing post-production on Man of Tomorrow. That, combined with what a public relations nightmare it would be to shelve a film like this, makes it clear that Man of Tomorrow will still arrive in theaters next summer.

Could It Get Batgirl’d? No, but don’t be surprised if this is the last film in the series.

This is another one that just has to come out at this point. Director Matt Reeves had to leave the production due to personal matters, with Steven Soderbergh coming in to help finish off principal photography. And this after an extremely lengthy development period – the first film, The Batman , came out in 2022, and after several delays the sequel currently has a February 18, 2028 release date.

But one does not simply cancel a Robert Pattinson Batman movie, even if, as IGN’s Jim Vejovda points out, it is increasingly feeling like this series very well could just end with this film . No, The Batman Part II will hit theaters, meaning the amount of time it took to make will have outdone Gunn and Safran’s tenure by about two years.

Could It Get Batgirl’d? A direct to HBO Max release doesn’t seem out of the realm.

This is one of those projects that we simply don’t know all that much about. Currently expected to be released in 2028, Dynamic Duo has been reported to be an origin story for two different Robins – Dick Grayson and Jason Todd. Additionaly, the film is expected to be made via “animation, puppetry, CGI, and live-action performance.” It was recently reported that The Black Phone’s Mason Thames had been cast in the film as Dick Grayson, while Ghostbusters: Afterlife’s Logan Kim will voice Jason Todd.

That said, while this certainly sounds like it could be a cool and visually interesting project, it also feels like Gunn and Safran pushing the boundaries a bit on what a standard studio superhero release might be. One could see this film, which is being produced by the relatively unknown Swaybox Studios, eventually being released directly to HBO Max instead of in theaters. Hopefully that’s not what happens, but we’ll see…

Mister Miracle and Creature Commandos Season 2

These are a pair of animated series that have been in active production for a while, with Mister Miracle featuring, as Safran told IGN last month, the voices of Josh Hutcherson as Scott Free and Mackenzie Davis as Big Barda . Eisner-winning writer Tom King has written all eight episodes of the series himself, based on his 2017 Mister Miracle comics series.

As for Creature Commandos , the first season already streamed on HBO Max in 2024 as the first title released in the Gunn/Safran DCU. The series was renewed for a Season 2 at the end of 2024, which means production has likely been underway for quite some time at this point. (Indeed, Gunn said on social media a few months ago that it is “long in production.” ) It would be surprising if the studio didn’t see these two series through to completion at this point in the process.

A lot of folks were surprised by the announcement of this show, which stars Skyler Gisondo as Jimmy Olsen in what is reportedly a riff on a true-crime TV series. It traces, obviously, the DC supervillain known as Gorilla Grodd and whether or not he was wrongfully convicted of a crime he did not commit. And yes, Gorilla Grodd is a gorilla . And he talks.

Sounds fun, right? And also weird and off-kilter and maybe not what a lot of superhero fans who are waiting for Batman and Wonder Woman to show up in the DCU might have really been excited to see next? So is a true-crime docu-series about a talking gorilla what new DC boss Jeremy Latcham wants under his tenure? Presumably it wasn’t a terribly expensive show to produce, and it’s already shot, so it will likely still get its HBO Max run. But don’t hold your breath for a People v. Condiment King Season 2 either.

Could It Get Batgirl’d? Yes, though it’s a bit of a different situation.

Lanterns became increasingly buzzy over the course of its first season, and it was also a show with a high enough pedigree that “normies” seemed to be watching it in addition to diehard comics fans. Starring Kyle Chandler as Hal Jordan and Aaron Pierre as John Stewart, both Green Lanterns, the series offered storytelling swerves and some really cool world-building – even while frustrating some viewers with its willingness to kill off the Hal Jordan character, who is typically considered the preeminent Lantern of DC comics.

A second season has never been officially greenlit, but we do know that a writers room was formed to work out ideas for a potential return. Safran told IGN recently that a decision would be made by the end of this year regarding whether Season 2 happens or not . He specifically talked about Pierre, who is appearing next in Man of Tomorrow. “We introduced him in Lanterns, and audiences will see him next summer in Man of Tomorrow,” said Safran. “So, it's really important to us in continuing to tell aspects of the story that we're not telling in the feature film world, so there's more to come.”

The thing is, Lanterns also felt like it had a natural end, Pierre returning for the Superman sequel notwithstanding. So the question becomes, why would the new regime want to invest more time and effort into a show that was kind of polarizing and which hasn’t shot a frame of film yet?

Could It Get Batgirl’d? Oh yes, though again, it’s not really a 1:1 situation.

Originally announced as part of Gunn and Safran’s initial “Gods and Monsters” plan for DC, The Brave and the Bold was meant to bring a different take on Batman to the big screen that would not conflict with Matt Reeves and Robert Pattinson’s The Batman (which of course is set in a different universe anyway). “Everybody knows I love Batman and it’s important to me so I’m working very closely with the writer on Brave and the Bold,” Gunn said last February. More recently, he teased in his The Suicide Squad: Is It Canon? podcast that it wouldn’t be “too long” before the DCU Batman was cast .

Unfortunately, now it seems like it will be very long before he’s cast – or at least, until the version Gunn had in mind is cast. Like, forever long. With Batman being such a key character for any DC universe, be it on the printed page, in animation, in games, or on the big screen, it seems likely that the new DC Studios powers that be, led by Latcham, will want to get their hands on whatever this film was going to be and turn it into something that they can claim as their own. New studio bosses are rarely fond of outgoing studio bosses’ projects, and they certainly don’t want to be outdone by them or want their predecessors to be able to claim success after they’re gone. No, it’s safe to say that The Brave and the Bold will cease to exist in whatever form it has held up until this point, and that an entirely new DCU Batman will appear from the entirely new DC Studios regime.

But what do you think of these projects’ chances of making it to the screen? Let’s discuss in the comments!

Talk to Scott Collura @scottcollura.bsky.social , or listen to his Star Trek podcast, Transporter Room 3 . Or do both!

articles.title: Peak Design’s Roller Lite Carry-On is bigger on the inside — and cheaper, too
articles.summary: Peak Design’s Roller Lite Carry-On ditches modular extras for a durable clamshell, 38 liters of space, and a $449 price tag.
articles.body: When we sampled Peak Design’s Roller Pro last year, we loved almost everything about the camera gear powerhouse’s first attempt at a proper suitcase. Everything, that is, except for the price. Back then, during its crowdfunded launch, the Pro could be had for as little as $425. Today, you’re looking at $599.95 for the same roller bag. Peak Design has taken that feedback to heart in creating the Roller Lite Carry-On, part of a new series of suitcases that bring many of the Pro’s features and design concepts into a hard-sided clamshell design that’s more traditional and, crucially, more affordable, starting with the $449.95 Lite Carry-On. It’s part of a new Lite family of suitcases. The slightly larger Lite Carry-On Plus costs $469.99 and measures 22.5 x 15 x 9 inches, while the $549.95 Lite Trunk is 30 x 16.1 x 13.8 inches. The former should still squeeze in most overhead compartments, while the latter is better off checked. Both, though, come in cheaper than the Pro. That cost-cutting does result in bags with fewer features and less originality, but I still found the new Lite Carry-On to be a great travel companion, first for a two-day whirlwind journey to Rome, then for a week in Tucson, Arizona. [Image: [Image: [Image: [Image: [Image: [Image: [Image: I travel a lot, spending far more time escorting my carry-on around airports than I do driving my car at home, so no surprise that I’m picky about what I drag through terminals and haul up into overhead compartments. I wouldn’t say that aesthetics are a primary concern, but everybody prefers a good-looking suitcase, and the Roller Lite passes that first test. It’s understated yet sophisticated in black, but the emerald green option called cypress might be even better. There’s also a hue called stone for those more into earth tones. Regardless of color, I think the Lite Carry-On’s hard plastic shell looks better than the soft-sided Roller Pro, and I’d hazard a guess it’ll stand the test of time better, too. The second trip I took with the Lite started in a tiny puddle-jumper of a plane. The flight attendant gate-checked any bag with wheels, even though the Lite Carry-On (21.7 x 13.8 x 9 inches, slightly smaller than the Pro) would have easily fit in the overhead. It came back to me from its trip to the belly of the aircraft with a few new scuffs and scratches, otherwise looking only a little worse for wear. --- Specs * Expandable from 38L to 45L. * 21.7 x 13.8 x 9 inches (55 x 35 x 22.9cm) and 7 pounds (3.2kg). * Spinner wheels designed for easy replacement when they wear out. * Dual zipper and TSA-approved lock. * The thin, space-saving carbon fiber handle helps to maximize interior space. * Handle expands to lock at 90 or 100cm. * Global carry-on compliant. * Integrated grab handles on the top, bottom, and both sides. * Backed by Peak Design’s lifetime warranty. --- Durability was a big selling point on the Roller Pro, and that continues here. The Lite is even more repairable thanks to its easily replaced strap handles. They sit flush without taking up any room in the suitcase itself, yet are quite comfortable to use. Both the Pro and Lite share the same carbon fiber handle, also easily replaceable. It’s my favorite feature, rising smoothly and dropping into place without a hitch. I especially love the dry carbon weave that’s exposed when it’s raised. My only complaint is that the handle on top is too bulky, making it a clumsy fit through the luggage passthrough on my backpack. But otherwise, the carbon construction makes for a sturdier feel than the handle on my Tumi 19 Degree Aluminum roller, which costs three times as much. While both share the same handle, the Lite’s design is a substantial departure from the Pro. The Pro offered a so-called “hybrid” layout, with the top opening up and swinging back into a single large compartment. The Lite is a more traditional clamshell with a zipper running the full circumference, splitting the case in two like a book. When it comes to packing camera equipment and other gear, I think the Pro’s single main compartment is easier to live with, especially if you’re hauling some bulky telephoto glass. [Image: [Image: [Image: [Image: [Image: [Image: [Image: But when I’m packing more items of clothing than camera gear, I actually prefer the Lite Carry-On’s two smaller compartments. I can separate clothes from everything else, which is useful when living out of a suitcase. The Lite Carry-On lacks the Pro’s trick external pockets for laptops, passports, and the like. That doesn’t bother me, as that stuff always goes in my backpack, but if you’re looking for a single-bag travel experience, the Pro is better suited. The Lite is also missing the Cord Hook feature of the Pro, potentially useful for strapping a tripod or the like to the outside. Inside, the right half of the Lite has a zippered flap cover with two large mesh pockets that don’t look or feel as good as the inner pockets on the Pro. You’ll still find a hidden pocket for tucking away an Apple AirTag tracker, though. The other side has the same elastic-strap holding system as the Pro. You load it up with stuff, then stretch the two hooks across to latch on the other side. It’s a basic, flimsy-looking solution, but it works. When the agents at Leonardo da Vinci International Airport wanted to rummage around in my bag, those little bungee hooks kept everything from scattering over the floor in Fiumicino. [Product: Peak Design Roller Lite Carry-On | The Lite Carry-On has an integrated, TSA-approved lock, something missing on the Pro, and though it’s slightly smaller on the outside (21.7 x 13.8 vs. 21.8 x 14), removing that front pocket makes it substantially bigger on the inside: 38 liters vs. 34 on the Pro, expanding to 45 liters vs. 39. The 2-inch expansion on the Lite is a great emergency solution if you picked up a few too many souvenirs in Seville, but the Lite feels loose and floppy when rolling around with its expansion zipper open. I don’t recommend it. Otherwise, when fully zipped and packed, I really enjoyed wheeling the Roller Lite around. It was an easy glider over smooth terminal floors and didn’t rattle obnoxiously over rougher asphalt. The Roller Lite Carry-On is undoubtedly a simpler suitcase than the Roller Pro that preceded it, and because of that, it doesn’t feel nearly as special to use or purpose-driven as Peak Design’s offerings typically are. But then it’s $150 cheaper, roomier, is easier to pack, and, in my estimation, will prove even more durable. It may not be the ultimate roller bag for pro photogs, but it’s my new favorite suitcase for under $500. I’d even put it ahead of options from Tumi, Briggs & Riley, and others that cost many times more, aren’t as easily repaired, and don’t come with a lifetime warranty. Photography by Tim Stevens / The Verge

articles.title: Is the DC Cinematic Universe Just Cursed?
articles.summary: Is the DC Cinematic Universe just cursed? Because it sure feels like it after James Gunn and Peter Safran's departure from DC Studios.
articles.body:
A hell of a way to start the news week, huh Captain? Barely a full month after Paramount Skydance closed their acquisition of Warner Bros. Discovery, we have news that James Gunn and Peter Safran are exiting as the heads of DC Studios. Whether you were a fan of Gunn’s approach to DC’s characters or not, announcing a full slate of film and television series only to be forced out four years later with several projects midway through development is a hell of a way to end things. While we don’t know if the DCU will continue or will be rebooted yet again under new head Jeremy Latcham (Gunn is apparently still attached to write one more DC project after his Superman sequel Man of Tomorrow is released), the shake-up indicates that Gunn’s plans will not survive in their current form.

Given how many times DC’s film strategy has changed over the past decade, I can’t help but ask: is the DC Cinematic Universe just cursed? Will we ever see a stable version of DC’s world on the big screen, or will it forever live in the shadow of the MCU? Let’s get into it.

When Gunn and Safran took control of DC Studios, there was no denying that the franchise was in the gutter. The first Wonder Woman and Aquaman films may have been financially successful, but Zack Snyder and Joss Whedon’s clashing visions of Justice League led to the main throughline of the series being a trainwreck that left subsequent projects struggling to pick up the pieces. This led to a string of films that were all box office disappointments or outright flops, including Birds of Prey, Black Adam, Shazam! Fury of the Gods, The Flash, and Blue Beetle. There were so many failures in a row that it’s hard to rationalize how the brand managed to stay alive.

Gunn’s entrance was seen by many as a much-needed injection of fresh blood, even if he already had DC experience with The Suicide Squad and the Peacemaker spin-off series. He started off strong with his Superman reboot, which isn’t perfect but got the fundamentals right with a good cast, an optimistic tone, and a fantastic take on Lex Luthor. Yet Gunn’s idiosyncrasies came back to bite him; his love for C-list characters and incessant quirkiness sparked backlash from fans who wondered why he was developing projects about Gorilla Grodd and Krypto while major heroes like Batman and Wonder Woman were nowhere to be seen. The reveal that Gunn even considered a Polka-Dot Man prequel show shortly before this week’s news is hard not to read as hilariously ironic.

However you feel about Gunn’s DC output, the biggest strike against him was that he’d already helmed projects in the previous DCEU, because it made the DCU’s new canon difficult to parse. Warners wanted to reboot the franchise, but Gunn was never going to throw his own film out of continuity, or get rid of the actors he personally liked (or was married to). It was hard not to roll my eyes when we learned that “aspects” of The Suicide Squad and Peacemaker were canon to the DCU while the rest of the DCEU was kicked out of continuity. Gunn even had to host a “Is It Canon?” podcast about his own work to clarify the issue, which led to bizarre statements like him being unsure whether the Joker exists in the DCU yet at the same time he claimed that Margot Robbie was welcome to reprise her role as Harley Quinn if she wanted it.

At the end of the day, a majority of Gunn’s plans for DC will never see fruition. He started this enterprise with a highly ambitious (and now we know, overly presumptuous) “Chapter One” plan involving 10 film and television projects, more than half of which were either cancelled or trapped in development hell when the shake-up was announced. It’s a sad state of affairs, but unfortunately for DC, hardly an unprecedented one.

Fans of the comics hoped that Gunn’s vision for the DCU would help move the Justice League and their friends away from the constant controversy of previous adaptations. Instead, the DCU repeated a pattern of upheaval and second-guessing that went all the way back to Man of Steel in 2013. Zack Snyder’s conception of Superman was polarizing to say the least, intended to launch a competitor to the Marvel Cinematic Universe that instead left many audiences cold to his dour and violent take on DC’s heroes ( though it certainly had its fans too ). That situation only worsened with the disastrous reception to Batman v Superman: Dawn of Justice, the critical and audience reception of which left the DCEU in a ditch at the same time the MCU was soaring to new heights. Just like Gunn, Snyder’s plan was ambitious, with a five-film arc that was supposed to include three Justice League movies, only to be cratered halfway through when the studio hired Joss Whedon to reshoot and remix the first Justice League film halfway through production.

The rest is history: Justice League came and went as little more than a blip in the wave of superhero movies, its only lasting relevance to the franchise being how much Snyder devotees yelled about it until they received his four-hour assembly cut in 2021. The next gambit was to reboot the series by using the Flash movie as a vehicle, adapting the time travel story Flashpoint to reset whatever the studio felt wasn’t working about the DCEU. But The Flash became another headache on its own, with a revolving door of directors and writers attached to the project, including Seth Grahame-Smith, Rick Famuyiwa, and John Francis Daley and Jonathan Goldstein before Andy Muschietti finally got it across the finish line. That’s not even getting into how the movie’s release became a public relations nightmare when lead actor Ezra Miller went on a cross-state crime spree and the third act committed ghoulish CGI necromancy of deceased actors like Christopher Reeve, Adam West, and George Reeves.

The amount of jaw-dropping DCEU behind-the-scenes lore is honestly impressive. One of the biggest movie studios on the face of the Earth (before they were absorbed into the Skydance conglomerate) kept trying to make a family friendly blockbuster entertainment franchise while dealing with situations like CEO Kevin Tsujihara resigning in 2019 after being caught soliciting sexual favors from actress Charlotte Kirk in exchange for acting jobs, Cyborg actor Ray Fisher accusing Whedon and DC’s corporate leadership, including Tsujihara’s replacement Walter Hamada, of creating a hostile and racist work environment, and Dwayne “The Rock” Johnson allegedly leaking falsified financial information to the press in an attempt to trick people into thinking Black Adam wasn’t a box office bomb. That last one even involved Johnson trying to take advantage of the power vacuum before Gunn’s hiring was finalized by bringing Henry Cavill back as Superman for Black Adam’s post-credits scene, only for Cavill to have to publicly share that he was once again departing the role two months later.

With all that and how many DCEU films were announced and subsequently cancelled (RIP Ben Affleck’s Batman solo movie), is it really any wonder that DC’s movie universe has never come close to the same cultural resonance as Marvel’s? But now that we know there’s another change of leadership coming, the biggest question coming out the other side of Gunn’s tenure is: will the next era be any different?

Whatever Happens to the Man of Tomorrow?

The next major release for the DCU is Gunn’s Superman sequel, Man of Tomorrow. The director will stay with the project through post-production, but with Latcham taking over as head of DC films, what was once supposed to be a pillar of Gunn’s universe will now be a eulogy. In the same way that The Flash wound up serving as a disappointing finale for the DCEU, fans are now going into Man of Tomorrow knowing that it’s the end of Gunn’s vision for the DCU instead of whatever he originally intended it to be. The constant reshuffling of leadership means that like The Flash before it, Man of Tomorrow is in a position of trying to set up new heroes and storylines after we already know they likely won’t go anywhere. What’s the point of getting invested in DC’s attempts at ongoing continuity if they’re just going to be reset and recast in a few years time, assuming they’re not cancelled entirely like Leslie Grace’s ill-fated Batgirl movie?

James Gunn's Man of Tomorrow: Superman vs. Lex Luthor Art Gallery

To be fair, it’s possible that Latcham will keep the current DCU going and not force us to sit through another reboot. IGN’s Jesse Schedeen made the argument that throwing out Gunn’s universe would be a mistake given how recently we wrapped up the last version. But new leadership rarely steps in without ideas of their own, which means the fates of Gunn’s characters are up in the air. Will DC really just settle for Kyle Chandler’s Hal Jordan being dead if they want to revive the Green Lantern franchise? Will Tom Rhys Harries’ Clayface actually get to meet the next incarnation of Batman? What happens if the next round of talent Latcham hires have their own casting ideas for characters Gunn has already selected, like with Adria Arjona rumored to be taking over the role of Wonder Woman in Man of Tomorrow? They’re lucky Gunn hasn’t cast his brother Sean as the Joker yet!

This of course brings up another argument that has been made over the years: that fans and the press should stop treating superhero projects as pieces of a bigger universe and instead as individual works. I get the idea, I do, but the flaw in that line of thinking is that these things are not conceived as individual projects anymore. Since the MCU’s success, virtually all superhero adaptations are produced and marketed as chapters of wider franchises, whether it’s Sony’s supervillain spin-offs, their Spider-Verse projects, or the DCU. Even standalone movies like Matt Reeves’ The Batman are still part of the same cinematic universe experiment, with spin-offs like the Penguin show at HBO Max and being referred to as “The Batman Epic Crime Saga.” Asking moviegoers who check out Man of Tomorrow to shut off the part of their brain that knows a lot of what Gunn develops in it may be changed is giving the people making these things credence they’re not actually due.

We’ll see where DC goes next once the last vestiges of Gunn’s reign are released. But if DC ever wants to not be second fiddle to the competition, they need to understand that constant upheaval has poisoned the well of audience goodwill. After all, it’s impossible to build something sturdy when the foundation’s always falling out from under you.

Carlos Morales has been writing about sci-fi and comic book movies since 2019, and has read 10,000 comics. You can follow his fixations on Twitter .

articles.title: The Witcher 3’s New Expansion Has Me Wondering if BioWare Should Have Focused on Dragon Age and Mass Effect DLC Rather Than Big New Games
articles.summary: The Witcher 3's Songs of the Past expansion has me wondering: what if BioWare had returned to its older games and made new expansions?
articles.body:
This is an opinion piece from writer Jess Kinghorn. IGN's opinion columns represent the personal viewpoints of the writer, drawing on their own experiences and research to explore the exciting world of video games.

Unless you’ve been camping out on some far flung space rock, you’ll have heard that EA shut down BioWare last month . 50 developers lost their jobs, and Mass Effect 5 was cancelled . It’s a disappointing end for the studio so foundational to the modern RPG.

BioWare’s final years were plagued by lengthy, troubled development cycles and messy final products. I’m left wondering what could’ve been – particularly when fellow genre titan CD Projekt Red continues to find success updating Cyberpunk 2077 and has even announced a new expansion to the decade-old The Witcher 3. Could BioWare have found a more secure future by developing expansions for its older, more beloved games rather than struggling on with Dragon Age: The Veilguard and Mass Effect 5?

Songs of the Past will be the third expansion for The Witcher 3: Wild Hunt and by the time it drops in 2027, the original will be 12 years old. I don’t know about you but back in 2015 I was going out of my gourd over every fresh revelation throughout Life Is Strange’s first season, and making Undertale my entire personality. Point being, that might as well be ancient in video game years.

Add to that The Witcher 3 Remastered , Cyberpunk 2077 2.0, plus its Phantom Liberty DLC, as well as the brand new Edgerunners Season 2 update, and it’s clear to see CD Projekt Red always has the long term success of its games top of mind. Remasters and DLC not only fill the boots of existing fans, but no doubt charm gamers new to these realms. All of it leaves me longingly looking at my copy of Mass Effect Legendary Edition, wondering what could have been for BioWare.

Mass Effect has always been at its best delivering snappy, episodic adventures in the mold of classic TV shows like Farscape (big up my sexy blue ladies). The Legendary Edition, launched in 2021, could have been the start of a new era for the original trilogy, introducing a steady trickle of new missions, DLC packs, or perhaps even a CDPR-style expansion which would have kept the series front of mind. Who would say no to, for instance, a fresh string of missions revolving around The Shadow Broker - especially as the studio had seemed keen to lean on Liara hype to stoke interest in future entries (again: big up).

But instead of continuing to build on what Mass Effect fans already loved, the studio was locked into working the live service mines for a completely different sci fi project, Anthem . Following a troubled 2019 release, the game was completely shut down earlier this year . The ripple effects of Anthem’s misfire would be felt throughout the rest of BioWare’s existence. Case in point, Dragon Age: The Veilguard . Work on the original incarnation of this devisive RPG began about a decade ago, before being rebooted in 2017 as a live service game built with Anthem’s development tools . To be fair, the live service model is one way to sustain storytelling in an established setting, though this was not the fate fans had wanted for the world of Thedas.

The project was officially unveiled as Dragon Age: Dreadwolf in 2022 , promising a conclusion to the arc of a certain bad boy elf in Dragon Age: Inquisition and its Trespasser DLC. The project was ultimately retooled as a single-player experience and released as Dragon Age: The Veilguard in 2025, a game that feels distinctly at war with itself .

Imagine a world where the Dreadwolf wasn’t sidelined in the very game that once carried his name. Imagine instead that my female elf inquisitor had been able to have the last word with everyone’s favourite evil egg years ago in one last massive hurrah for Inquisition, an expansion that had the space and focus to conclude the base game’s many threads. Imagine The Veilguard had been properly free to tell a new story all its own.

Instead, the ending The Veilguard offers us Solas romancers is… mostly fine. But, at the risk of skirting some major spoilers, I’ve no doubt it would have been all the more impactful to be in the driver’s seat rather than watching some NPCs walk off into the sunset. It’s yet another example of the weird clash at the heart of The Veilguard: it explores the northern reaches of Thedas for the first time, while the story is still trying to wrap up everything that went on down south.

After all of Tresspasser’s set up, chasing Solas through The Veilguard's flashy opening ends up feeling like I’ve skipped over a whole other Dragon Age game. Hastily punting the bald baddie into the Fade and introducing new villains feels like a lapse of judgement, misunderstanding what fans were looking for after following this story across so many years. Inquisition and Veilguard launched 10-years apart (with The Trespasser DLC dropping just one year after Inquisition). Is it really too offbase an idea to suggest that 2014's award-sweeping megahit could have gotten more DLC releases to bridge the gap? If games like The Witcher 3 can still get its hooks in with a new expansion, it seems like a massive missed opportunity here.

It’s hard not to see 2017’s Mass Effect: Andromeda as a similarly troubled false start. The Legendary Edition remaster could’ve been a fantastic platform for original space-faring stories with established characters. Unfortunately, BioWare began development on yet another fresh start taking place hundreds of years after Mass Effect 3 instead. As this project was cancelled with the studio’s closure, Andromeda’s infamy is left to linger over the series’ legacy like its very own accursed veil.

As nostalgia is not a particularly deep well to draw from, each attempt to reinvent BioWare’s RPG wheels are at least understandable. Still, pivoting a beloved RPG studio to live service games will forever remain a headscratcher. It’s hard not to wonder what could’ve been if BioWare had been allowed to tell smaller scope follow up stories instead – would the studio have avoided being on EA’s chopping block altogether? By all rights BioWare should have been in a position to match Baldur's Gate 3’s success, rather than see that particular hype train and the wider genre revival chug along right past them.

It’s clear EA didn’t know what it had with BioWare . The studio we knew is gone – though perhaps not completely dead if recent comments made by Canadian MP Don Davies in response to a fanmade petition are any indication. If BioWare’s laid off developers are able to ‘buy back their studio’, here’s hoping it's the fresh start that finally sticks the landing. In the meantime, the spirit of BioWare lives on in plenty of RPGs - though with former staff involved in Exodus , maybe evolution is more likely than a resurrection.

Jess Kinghorn is a freelancer writer who has written for PC Gamer, PLAY, and GamesRadar+.

articles.title: GTA 6 Is Now Available to Pre-Load on PS5 and Xbox Series X|S
articles.summary: You can now preload Grand Theft Auto 6 onto your PS5 or Xbox Series X|S. But you still have to wait until November 19 to play it.
articles.body:
The day has come: if you’ve preordered Grand Theft Auto 6 , you can now preload the game onto your PS5 or Xbox Series X|S. You’ll need 212GB of space on your drive , but if you have the free storage space, you can load the game onto your console so it’s ready to go when it releases on November 19 (you can check your global release time here ).

If you preordered a "physical copy," you’ll have to wait until it arrives to preload it, but it should be delivered within the next few days. I use scare quotes on the words "physical copy" because there is no actual disc version of GTA 6. Physical copies are simply a box that includes a code you can redeem on the PlayStation Store or Xbox Store.

Those who haven’t preordered a copy can do so now and begin their preload. It’s available in two editions: standard and ultimate. The ultimate edition comes with a bunch of extra in-game digital items, detailed below.

Physical copies of GTA 6 are only available for the standard edition. But, if you want a box to put on your shelf and you also want the ultimate edition, you can buy the physical standard edition, and then buy the "Ultimate Edition Upgrade," which basically turns your standard edition into the ultimate edition. The total cost is the same.

Here are all the preorder links you'll need, in case you haven't locked in your preorder yet but want to jump on it now that preloads are live.

Grand Theft Auto VI is now confirmed as the most pre-ordered game in history on both the PlayStation Store (according to the official PlayStation Blog ) and the Microsoft Store (according to Microsoft's official Xbox Wire ). That's perhaps unsurprising, both because it's probably the most highly anticipated game ever released, and because physical copies only exist in "code in a box" form. Even so, it's impressive.

articles.title: GTA 6 'Preload Now' Trailer Includes Nearly 30 Seconds of New Footage — SWAT Team, Nightclub Dancing, and More
articles.summary: Rockstar has released a new GTA 6 trailer announcing the launch of preloads, and it includes nearly 30 seconds of new footage.
articles.body:
Rockstar has released a new GTA 6 trailer announcing the launch of preloads, and it includes new footage.

Preloading is now available for everyone who has preordered GTA 6 digitally (those who preordered the code-in-the-box version can also activate their code and begin preloading as soon as it’s received).

Rockstar has also, finally, announced the performance specifications GTA 6 is shooting for across PlayStation 5, PlayStation 5 Pro, Xbox Series X and S, and even Xbox One, but our focus here is the accompanying new trailer. While it’s only 29 seconds long, it does include snippets of never-before-seen footage, which has already got fans talking.

The trailer, which features ‘Blood in Your Eyes’ by Tove Lo from Grand Theft Auto VI: The Album, starts with the “Plays Best on PS5” message we’ve seen on pretty much all the GTA 6 marketing material so far, per Sony’s partnership with Rockstar Games. We then see Lucia and Jason dancing together in a nightclub, before we switch to a racetrack in the daytime, where Lucia watches an enthusiastic driver do a backflip.

We then switch to a character saying, “I mean, it’s not really my thing, you know what I’m sayin’?” This is music producer Dre'Quan Priest (“Now that he's signed the Real Dimez, Dre'Quan's days of booking acts into Boobie's strip club might be numbered as he sets his sights on the Vice City scene.”)

We then see Jason push someone into a shower (I think it’s a shower!), a party on a boat called “Ships And Giggles,” and then something interesting: a SWAT team that looks like it’s responding to an emergency of some sort. My best guess is these guys are part of the team that assaulted the building Jason and Lucia escape from in the Extended Look.

We then see Lucia and a friend getting ready for a night out, before another character makes a dramatic exit, saying, “Oh, it is so on now!”
